assertions_contracts.best_practice: Bash has no native assert; explicit guards are the standard substitute
assertions_contracts.evidence: No primary source contradicts; guide correctly notes no optimizer strips shell guards
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Explicit [[ ... ]] || die guards for invariants and external validation; header/function contracts

bounded_work.best_practice: No official bash guidance contradicts bounded subprocess/input work; it remains the recognised hardening pattern
bounded_work.evidence: Guide rules align with bash manual semantics for timeout-adjacent coreutils use as described; no primary source fetched contradicts them
bounded_work.guide_position: Named UPPER_SNAKE bounds for timeouts, bytes, retries, loop counts, find depth; timeout/PIPESTATUS discipline

concurrency.best_practice: Still sound; the guide now also documents the bash 5.3 change (wait -n waiting on process substitutions) that scripts relying on wait should re-check
concurrency.evidence: Bash 5.3 announce lists wait -n returning terminated process substitutions and related job-notification changes; guide section 2 now names that addition explicitly
concurrency.guide_position: Track PIDs, wait for background jobs, bound job count; distinguish timeout 124

error_handling.best_practice: Explicit checks remain best practice; errexit is disabled by default inside command substitution for function invocations unless inherit_errexit (bash 4.4+) is set, per ShellCheck SC2311; ERR traps need set -E/errtrace to be inherited by functions and subshells
error_handling.evidence: Run-1 stale verdict remediated and verified in the current text: section 3 now states a failing command in a command substitution does NOT reliably trigger -e (with the inherit_errexit remedy named), and a separate section 3 paragraph states an ERR trap is not inherited unless set -E (errtrace) is set explicitly
error_handling.guide_position: set -euo pipefail plus explicit checks; section 3 now correctly states errexit does not reliably fire in command substitution for function invocations, names shopt -s inherit_errexit as the remedy, and covers set -E (errtrace) for ERR-trap inheritance

formatting.best_practice: shfmt remains the standard bash formatter; a single pinned flag set should be used consistently
formatting.evidence: Run-1 internal inconsistency remediated and verified in the current text: SKILL.md and guide section 26 now both prescribe shfmt -i 4 -ci -bn
formatting.guide_position: One formatter: shfmt, 4-space indent, -ci -bn; SKILL.md and the full guide now agree on the full flag set

memory_ownership.best_practice: Does not apply: bash has no memory-ownership system
memory_ownership.evidence: Aspect does not apply to a shell language; nearest analogue (resource cleanup) is covered under bounded_work/error_handling
memory_ownership.guide_position: No ownership model; guide instead covers temp-file ownership, cleanup traps and subprocess reaping

security.best_practice: Unchanged official/community best practice; ShellCheck SC2251/SC2311 family reinforces explicit status handling over blind errexit trust
security.evidence: Guide bans match ShellCheck-documented failure modes; no primary source contradicts the bans
security.guide_position: No eval, no curl|bash, checksum verification, mktemp only, -- before user paths, env/PATH distrust, no secrets in argv

static_analysis.best_practice: ShellCheck remains actively maintained (0.11.0 is still the newest release as of this pass) and is the standard static analyser for bash/sh
static_analysis.evidence: Search of the upstream project in this pass confirms 0.11.0 (Aug 2025) is still the newest ShellCheck release; guide's zero-warning gate rests on it
static_analysis.guide_position: shellcheck zero warnings as a CI gate, justified suppressions only; bash-language-server for LSP

testing.best_practice: bats-core remains the standard bash test framework (1.14.0, Jul 2026); guide does not pin a version, so no stale pin
testing.evidence: bats-core's latest release is 1.14.0 per references fetched in this pass; the practice itself is uncontradicted and the guide pins no version that could go stale
testing.guide_position: bats for behaviour tests, half adversarial, hermetic mktemp dirs

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current stable is bash 5.3 (Jul 2025), now named by the guide as the preferred line; the guide's documented 5.3 additions match the GNU announce
toolchain_pins.evidence: Run-1 stale verdict remediated and verified in the current text: guide section 2 names Bash 5.3 (July 2025) as the current stable line and lists its current-shell substitution, GLOBSORT, source -p, and wait -n additions; SKILL.md compatibility now reads 'Bash 4.4+ (5.3 preferred)'. Two minor 5.3 additions from the run-1 proposal (trap -P, BASH_TRAPSIG) remain undocumented - carried as a residual proposal, not a stale pin
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Targets bash 4.4+ as the floor (unchanged guard), with 5.3 named as the preferred/current stable line in guide section 2 and SKILL compatibility; tool names paired without version pins

current_versions.bash: 5.3 (first public release 3-5 Jul 2025, GNU announce; patch releases continue on the 5.3 line)
current_versions.bash-language-server: 5.8.x line current (server-5.8.0 is the latest upstream release tag found in this pass); guide names the tool without a version pin
current_versions.bashdb: guide does not pin a version; current state not verified from a primary source in this pass
current_versions.bats: 1.14.0 (Jul 2026) is the latest bats-core release; guide does not pin a version
current_versions.shellcheck: 0.11.0 (Aug 2025) remains the newest release, per the upstream project in this pass
current_versions.shfmt: 3.14.1 (Sep 2026) is the latest mvdan/sh release found in this pass; guide pins flags, not a version

proposals.evidence: Residual of the run-1 re-baseline proposal: the main proposal landed in pass 2 (guide section 2 names 5.3 and documents ${| ...; }, GLOBSORT, source -p, and wait -n; verified in the current text), but trap -P and BASH_TRAPSIG appear nowhere in SKILL.md or the full guide
proposals.proposal: Document the two bash 5.3 additions from the run-1 proposal that the pass-2 re-baseline did not cover - trap -P and BASH_TRAPSIG - in the guide's 5.3 notes (sections 2/20 area), under the same bound-and-check discipline as the other documented 5.3 features
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a small completeness addition; the 5.3 re-baseline itself is done and should not be re-opened
